config.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync

intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API to share authentication state between tabs. The core concept involves listening for storage events to detect changes made in other tabs and updating your app's reactive state accordingly. You'll implement this by creating a Vue composable to manage the auth state and a component to display the login status. This will help you understand real-time state synchronization in a multi-tab environment using Vue's reactivity system.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently open multiple tabs. In banking dashboards, e-commerce sites, or collaborative tools like Google Workspace, logging out in one tab should immediately reflect across all open tabs to prevent security risks. This pattern ensures consistent authentication state in applications with real-time features like chat platforms or project management tools where session management is critical. Developers implement this to provide secure, seamless user experiences when switching between different views of the same application.

objectives: Implement a Vue composable to manage authentication state across browser tabs
Configure event listeners to detect authentication changes in other tabs
Initialize reactive authentication state that persists across tab sessions
Bind authentication state updates to localStorage synchronization
Construct a mechanism to broadcast authentication changes to other tabs
Integrate the multi-tab auth sync system into a Vue component
Manipulate authentication state and observe synchronized updates across tabs

steps.title: Initialize reactive authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your AuthSyncApp component, use the ref function to create a reactive state variable named isAuthenticated and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Remember that ref creates reactive references. You'll need to call ref(false) and assign it to a variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reactive isAuthenticated state variable that tracks whether the user is authenticated, starting with false.
successCriteria: The setup function contains a const isAuthenticated = ref(false) declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref() to create the reactive state and initializing it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating the reactive state. You need to use ref(false) to create a reactive variable named isAuthenticated inside the setup function.

steps.title: Create storage event handler for cross-tab sync
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleStorageChange that takes an event parameter and updates the isAuthenticated ref when the localStorage 'auth' key changes.
steps.hint: The function should check if event.key equals 'auth' and update isAuthenticated.value accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleStorageChange function that responds to storage events and updates authentication state.
successCriteria: A handleStorageChange function is defined inside setup, checks event.key, and updates isAuthenticated.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it checks event.key and updates isAuthenticated.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleStorageChange function is missing or doesn't properly handle storage events.

steps.title: Set up event listener for storage events
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, use the imported onMounted hook to add an event listener for 'storage' events on the window object, calling your handleStorageChange function. Also use onUnmounted to remove the same listener when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Remember to pass the same function reference to both addEventListener and removeEventListener.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now listen for storage events when mounted and stop listening when unmounted.
successCriteria: onMounted and onUnmounted hooks are used to add and remove a 'storage' event listener on window, calling handleStorageChange.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using both onMounted and onUnmounted, and that the event type is 'storage'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storage event listener isn't properly set up. Check that you're using onMounted and onUnmounted with window.addEventListener and window.removeEventListener.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named 'login' that sets isAuthenticated to true and stores the authentication state in localStorage.
steps.hint: Define a function that updates the reactive state and persists it to localStorage with a key like 'authState'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The login function will update the authentication state and persist it to localStorage, enabling cross-tab synchronization.
successCriteria: A function named 'login' is defined that sets isAuthenticated.value to true and calls localStorage.setItem with appropriate key/value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function sets isAuthenticated to true and stores the value in localStorage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or doesn't properly update state and localStorage.

steps.title: Create logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your component's setup function, create a logout handler function named 'logout' that sets isAuthenticated to false and updates localStorage with the new authentication state.
steps.hint: The function should update the reactive state and also persist the change to localStorage so other tabs can sync.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a logout function that updates both local state and localStorage, enabling cross-tab synchronization when logging out.
successCriteria: A function named 'logout' is defined that sets isAuthenticated to false and updates localStorage with the key 'auth' and value 'false'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a logout function, but make sure it both updates isAuthenticated.value and sets localStorage with key 'auth' and value 'false'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler is missing or doesn't properly update both the reactive state and localStorage.

steps.title: Add login button and wire it to the login handler
steps.instruction: In the template section of your component, add a button element with the text 'Login' and bind its click event to the login handler using @click.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call the login function when the button is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:

<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>

successCriteria: The template contains a button element with text 'Login' and an @click binding to the login function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
